The RGBlimp is a miniature robotic blimp that combines the desirable features of a robotic blimp and a fixed-wing glider.
The RGBlimp uses a helium-filled envelope for buoyant lift and a pair of wings for aerodynamic lift.
The RGBlimp adopts a moving mass for attitude control, inspired by the centroid control of flying squirrels in gliding.
The dynamic model of the RGBlimp considers the dynamic effects of the moving mass, which is often ignored in existing robotic blimp models.
The aerodynamic coefficients of the RGBlimp were identified using a series of steady flight tests with different displacements of the moving mass.
The RGBlimp model predictions matched the experimental data reasonably well for both steady straight-line and spiral flights.
The dynamic flight experiments showed that the proposed RGBlimp model could predict the flight trajectory, turning radius, and vertical speed, including both the powered and unpowered gliding phases.
The fixed wings of the RGBlimp prototype significantly improved the gliding performance compared to a conventional robotic blimp without wings.
The net weight of the RGBlimp prototype was 6.85g, and the dimensions were 1.0 x 1.1 x 0.5m.
The mass distribution of the RGBlimp included a helium-filled envelope (21.19g), a stationary body (104.81g), and a moving mass gondola (54.08g).
The RGBlimp design combines both buoyant and aerodynamic lift to achieve improved aerodynamic efficiency and stability compared to existing miniature robotic blimps.
The RGBlimp is the first miniature robotic blimp in the literature with moving mass control and hybrid buoyant-aerodynamic lift.
The RGBlimp adopts a pair of propellers for propulsion and yaw adjustment, and the moving mass for attitude control.
The RGBlimp dynamic model includes the Coriolis force and centrifugal force caused by the separation between the center of gravity and the center of buoyancy.
The aerodynamic force and moment coefficients of the RGBlimp were modeled as polynomial functions of the angle of attack and sideslip angle.
